data.title: Process Injection Not Detected
data.summary:
Code was injected into legitimate running processes and executed under their identity,
inheriting their trust and network permissions, without detection by endpoint protection.
data.description:
Injection moves attacker code inside a process the organisation trusts. Outbound
connections then originate from a signed, expected binary; application control rules that
permit that binary permit the injected code; and analysts reviewing process trees see
nothing unusual.

Detecting it depends on behavioural telemetry — cross-process memory operations, remote
thread creation, suspicious memory protections — rather than on file inspection, since no
malicious file need exist. Products differ widely in whether they collect this, and in
whether the collection is enabled in the deployed configuration.

Where injection succeeds silently, most subsequent detections are also unlikely, because
the activity is attributed to the host process.
data.recommendation:
* Confirm that the endpoint product's behavioural detection for cross-process operations is
  enabled, not merely licensed.
* Apply exploit protection to high-value processes — browsers, mail clients, office
  applications — to raise the cost of injection into them.
* Hunt for signed processes making network connections inconsistent with their function.
data.short_recommendation: Enable behavioural detection for cross-process operations and protect high-value processes.
